chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abi al-Jaroud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is nothing (specifically) prescribed to be performed upon Al-Safa.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims perform Sa'i
key_terms.مُوَقَّتٌ: Prescribed/Fixed, referring to a specific time, action, or formula that is obligatory or strictly defined

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed ritual for pausing upon Al-Safa during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that while pausing upon Al-Safa is a recommended act of worship, there is no specific, fixed ritual or supplication mandated by the Sharia for this particular pause. This ruling distinguishes the general recommendation of the act from the specific, obligatory rituals like Sa'i, highlighting the flexibility in devotional practices during Hajj and Umrah within Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Hassan Bin Abu Al Hassan Bin Abu Al Hassan, from Salih Bin Abu Al Aswad, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is nothing (specifically) Prescribed (to be performed) upon Al-Safa’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hassan ibn abu al-Hassan from Salih ibn abu al-Aswad from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There is no definite act of worship to perform on al-Safa’.’”
